real_defects.issue: parsePairs split a semicolon-separated file with decimal commas (Excel's CSV in most of Europe, e.g. '4,1;4,3') on the comma: with no header row it silently read x=5, y=4 instead of 5.0/5.4 for every row (first row eaten as a header); with a header it refused the file. Fix: semicolon on every one of the first 5 lines picks ';' and reads decimal commas.

analyze({x, y}) coerced with Number, so null, '' and false readings (a missing value in JSON from an agent or a script) became 0 and entered every fit with no warning. Fix: only numbers and numeric strings are readings; anything else throws.

analyze crashed with 'map is not a function' when decisionLevels was a single number or a string such as '120, 140', and kept null as a level of 0. Fix: accept a number, a list string or an array; drop non-numbers. First version of the fix split strings on commas and was caught by CI's check_thousands_split ('6,000' -> 6 and 0); now grouped tokens stay one number, and the page's level box (which had the same split) passes its text to the engine.

analyze({p, y}) mapped p with Number (null -> 0, a valid forecast) and counted every outcome other than true/1/'1' as a non-event, so y written 'yes'/'no' or with a null gave wrong calibration with no error. Fix: p via toNumber, y via toOutcome (the CSV reader's yes/no words); unreadable values throw.

analyze({t, y}) mapped with Number, so null/''/false times or values became 0 and passed the finite check. Fix: only numbers and non-empty strings are read; others fail 'Row N has a missing or bad number'.
